responses: Hello! How can I help you at the library today?
Hi there! Looking for a book or something else?
Good day! What can I help you find?
Goodbye! Happy reading.
See you next time!
Bye - enjoy your books.
You're very welcome!
Glad I could help.
Any time - that's what I'm here for.
I can help you join, search the catalogue, renew or reserve items, check fines, and tell you about our spaces and events.
Ask me about borrowing, renewals, reservations, opening times, computers, study rooms or events.
I'm the library's assistant bot, built with Python and TensorFlow. A librarian can help with anything I can't.
I'm an automated helper. For trickier questions, our librarians are at the front desk.

patterns: What time does the library shut?
responses: We're open 9am to 7pm Monday to Friday, 9am to 5pm Saturday, and 11am to 4pm Sunday.
Weekdays 9am until 7pm, weekends shorter. We close on bank holidays.

patterns: How do I get to the library?
Which bus goes to the library?
responses: We're on the high street opposite the town hall. There's a car park behind the building, free for two hours.
Ten minutes' walk from the station, and buses 4, 12 and 27 stop outside. Want directions?

patterns: How do I become a member?
What do I need to register?
How do I get a card?
responses: Joining is free. Bring proof of name and address, or start the form online and finish it at the desk.
You can sign up online in about five minutes, or come in with ID and we'll do it there and then.

patterns: How many books can I borrow?
How long can I keep a book?
How long do I have to read it?
responses: You can borrow up to 15 items for three weeks. DVDs and new releases are one week.
15 items at a time, three weeks each, renewable twice if nobody's reserved them.

patterns: I want to renew my books
I need more time with this book
Can I keep it another week?
responses: I can renew that for you. Items renew twice unless someone has reserved them.
Renewals are easy online, by phone, or here. Would you like me to renew everything on your account?

patterns: Where do I return my books?
How do I give the book back?
Can I return to a different branch?
Can I return books when you're closed?
responses: Return them at the desk, or use the 24-hour drop box by the main entrance.
Any branch will take them back, and the drop box outside works when we're closed.

patterns: I want to place a hold
Put a book on hold for me
How do I request a title?
Can you save a copy for me?
Add me to the waiting list
responses: Yes - reservations are free and we'll text you when it's ready to collect.
I can place a hold. You'll get a message when it arrives, and it's kept for a week.

patterns: Have you got anything by this author?
Where would I find history books?
I need a book about gardening
responses: I can search the catalogue. What's the title or author?
Tell me the title, author or subject and I'll check what's on the shelves.

patterns: I have a fine to pay
Can I pay my fine online?
responses: Late charges are 10p per item per day, capped at £5. Children's items have no charges at all.
I can check your balance. Fines are payable at the desk, online, or by card here.

patterns: I can't find the book I borrowed
What if I lose an item?
responses: It happens - let a librarian know and we'll work out a replacement cost. Please don't try to repair it yourself.
No drama. Bring it in or tell us at the desk and we'll sort a replacement charge.

patterns: Can I borrow without my card?
responses: We can issue a replacement for £2, and cancel the old one straight away so nobody else can use it.
Let us know as soon as possible and we'll block the old card. Photo ID is enough to borrow meanwhile.

patterns: How do I read on my Kindle?
Can I download books at home?
responses: Yes - ebooks, audiobooks, magazines and newspapers, all free with your card through our app.
Our digital collection works on phones, tablets and most e-readers. Want help setting it up?

patterns: Do I need to book a PC?
responses: Free wifi throughout, and public computers bookable in one-hour slots. Printing is 10p a page black and white.
Computers are free with your card. Printing, scanning and photocopying are all available at the desk.

patterns: Can I book a study room?
Do you have desks I can work at?
responses: We have a silent study floor and four bookable rooms for group work. Shall I check availability?
Plenty of desks with power sockets, plus a quiet floor upstairs. Rooms can be booked up to a week ahead.

patterns: Do you have a book club?
Is there story time for kids?
Are there activities in the holidays?
responses: We run story time, two book clubs, computer classes and regular author talks. Which interests you?
There's something most days. Want me to list this week's events?

patterns: Can you get a book from another library?
You don't have the book I need
Can you order it in for me?
Can you buy a book I suggest?
How do I get a title you don't stock?
responses: Yes - we can request it from another branch or library service. There's a small fee for items from outside the county.
We take purchase suggestions too. Give me the title and author and I'll pass it on.

patterns: Do you have a children's section?
Is there a summer reading challenge?
Books for a five year old
responses: The children's library is on the ground floor, and under-16s never pay late charges. Story time is Tuesday and Thursday mornings.
Children can join free from birth. We run the summer reading challenge and homework clubs after school.

patterns: Do you have large print books?
Can you deliver books to my home?
Do you have audiobooks for blind readers?
I can't get to the library easily
responses: Yes - large print, audiobooks, step-free access throughout and a hearing loop at the desk.
We run a free home delivery service for anyone who can't get in easily. Shall I put you in touch?

patterns: I want to speak to a librarian
Can I talk to a person?
responses: Of course - a librarian is at the front desk, or I can take a message.
I'll pass you to a person. The desk is staffed during all opening hours.
Sorry, I didn't catch that. Could you rephrase?
I'm not sure I follow - try asking a different way?
That one's beyond me. A librarian at the desk can help.
